note: On 31 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of the home of Mayor Ed Gainey in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call on the city to tackle the housing crisis and in support of unhoused people in the city.

On 29 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside of a printing plant in Clinton (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. The picket took place as part of a strike which started on 6 October 2022 organized, in part, by the Pittsburgh Typographical Union (an affiliate of the CWA) alongside the Pittsburgh News Guild.

On 27 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of the office of Sen. Pat Toomey in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator. State Sen. Tim Kearney (D) participated in the rally which was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey. At least one protestor held a sign in support of abortion.

On 22 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in a building near 48th and Osage Ave. in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call on Altman Management to address 'serious issues' with an apartment building overseen by the company, including an elevator which has been broken for two years despite the needs of disabled tenants. Tenants of the building and members of the Save UC Townhomes coalition (which is made up of Penn faculty, students, community members, and a Black group known as the Black Bottom Tribe) participated in the demonstration.

On 21 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of ICE Headquarters in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for the release of all the women detained in Berks Detention Center before the holidays. Members of CASA, Shut Down Berks Coalition, Free Migration Project, and Juntos participated in the demonstration.
On 20 December 2022, an unreported number of people rallied outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) as part of 'Tuesdays with Toomey' in opposition to the Senator.

On 20 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. State Rep. Sara Innamorato (D), Press Secretary for Pittsburgh Mayor Ed Gainey, and members of CWA Local 1168 AFL-CIO participated in the picket which took place as part of day 64 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 18 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside the 20th and Market St. Starbucks in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to 'understaffed stores, poor management,' and union-busting tactics employed by the chain. Members of Workers United PJB (affiliated with the SEIU) participated in the picket which took place as part of day 3 of a nationwide 3-day 'Double Down Strike' organized by Starbucks Workers United.

On 18 December 2022, about 30 people gathered in Binns Park in Lancaster (Pennsylvania) to call for state legislation to 'address access [to] and safety [of]' guns and to honor those who have died to gun violence in the city. At least one protester held a sign calling for a ban on assault rifles. Former Lancaster Mayor Rick Gray, a Christian pastor, and members of Ceasefire PA spoke at the vigil which was organized by Families Against Gun Violence and Heeding God's Call to End Gun Violence.

On 18 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside the Southside Starbucks in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in opposition to 'understaffed stores, poor management,' and union-busting tactics employed by the chain. Workers also picketed outside the East Carson store. The pickets took place as part of day 3 of a nationwide 3-day 'Double Down Strike' organized by Starbucks Workers United.

On 17 December 2022, four dozen people, including Bhutanese-Americans, rallied outside the Capitol in Harrisburg (Pennsylvania) to call for amnesty for political prisoners in Bhutan. The Global Campaign for the Release of Political Prisoners in Bhutan organized the rally.

On 17 December 2022, an unreported number of people rallied outside the 9th and South Starbucks in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to 'understaffed stores, poor management,' and union-busting tactics employed by the chain. Members of the Philadelphia Federation of Teachers (affiliated with the AFT) participated in the picket which took place as part of day 2 of a nationwide 3-day 'Double Down Strike' organized by Starbucks Workers United.

On 17 December 2022, 8 to 10 people picketed outside the McKnight Road Starbucks in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in opposition to 'understaffed stores, poor management,' and union-busting tactics employed by the chain. Workers also picketed outside the Market Square, South Hills Village, Southside, and Southbound stores. Members of the United Steelworkers participated in the pickets which took place as part of day 2 of a nationwide 3-day 'Double Down Strike' organized by Starbucks Workers United.

On 17 December 2022, an unreported number of people marched from the Luzerne County River Common to the Public Square in Wilkes-Barre (Pennsylvania) to call for justice and transparency regarding the death of man who died following an altercation at a local bar on 26 August and to honor his life. Members of the man's family participated in the rally.

On 16 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of the Juanita Kidd Stout Center for Criminal Justice in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for the release of a Black man who was convicted of killing a police officer in 1981.

On 16 December 2022, an unreported number of workers picketed outside the Penn Medicine Starbucks in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to 'understaffed stores, poor management,' and union-busting tactics employed by the chain. The picket took place as part of day 1 of a nationwide 3-day 'Double Down Strike' organized by Starbucks Workers United.

On 16 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. On 16 December 2022, an unreported number of workers picketed outside Starbucks stores in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in opposition to 'understaffed stores, poor management,' and union-busting tactics employed by the chain. The pickets took place as part of day 1 of a nationwide 3-day 'Double Down Strike' organized by Starbucks Workers United.

On 15 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. The picket took place as part of day 60 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 14 December 2022, a small group of people gathered in New Kensington (Pennsylvania) to call for the person responsible for the death of a Black man who was shot and killed in the city on 9 December to turn themselves in as well as to honor the victim's life and call for an end to gun violence. Members of the man's family as well as a Christian pastor participated in the vigil.

On 14 December 2022, about 30 students marched from the West Chester University campus to the home of the university's president in West Chester (Pennsylvania) to call on the university to tackle the lack of affordable housing options for students.

On 14 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. Other striking workers from the paper represented by Communications Workers of America Locals 14842 and 14827, Teamsters Local 205/211, and Pressmen's Union Local 24M/9N (which is a part of the Teamsters) joined the picket which took place as part of day 59 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 13 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) as part of 'Tuesdays with Toomey' in opposition to the Senator and his recent vote against the passage of money laundering legislation.

On 13 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. Members of the United Steelworkers joined the picket which took place as part of day 58 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 12 December 2022, 8 to 9 people demonstrated outside of the York County Courthouse in York (Pennsylvania) in support of a man who is currently undergoing a trial in the 2018 death of an infant. Demonstrators claim he is being wrongly accused and called for justice for the murdered infant.

On 12 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. The picket took place as part of day 57 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 10 December 2022, an unreported number of people gathered in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) to call for an end to gun violence as well as to honor the life of a Black man who was killed in a double homicide on 5 December. Members of the man's family participated in the vigil.

On 9 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. The picket took place as part of day 53 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 9 December 2022, an unreported number of people rallied outside of a Starbucks in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) in support of unionizing Starbucks workers nationwide and to call for Starbucks to bargain in good-faith with unionizing workers. State Rep. Dan Miller (D), State Sen. Lindsey Williams (D), and State Rep. Aerion Abney (D) as well as members of the Pennsylvania AFL-CIO, Allegheny-Fayette County Labor Council, 32BJ SEIU, Pride at Work (an LGBT+ organization), USW Local 3657, Pittsburgh Federation of Teachers (an affiliate of the AFT), and the Newspaper Guild of Pittsburgh (an affiliate of the CWA) participated in the rally which was organized by Starbucks Workers United in celebration of the one-year anniversary of the first Starbucks store to unionize.

On 8 December 2022, people demonstrated outside of the Philadelphia International Airport (Pennsylvania) to call on Congress to pass the 'Good Jobs for Good Airports Act' which would improve pay and other working conditions for airport workers. State Rep. Joe Hohenstein (D) participated in the demonstration which took place as part of a nationwide day of action organized by Airport Workers United.

On 7 December 2022, a small group of people demonstrated outside of the York County Judicial Center in York (Pennsylvania) in support of a man who is currently undergoing a trial in the 2018 death of an infant. Demonstrators claim he is being wrongly accused and called for justice for the murdered infant.

On 7 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. The picket took place as part of day 51 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 7 December 2022, about 75 faculty members demonstrated on the University of Pittsburgh campus in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for automatic contract renewal for non-tenured faculty members and an annual pay floor of $60,000 for full-time instructors. The faculty are represented by the Union of Pitt Faculty, an affiliate of the United Steelworkers.

On 7 December 2022, about 50 people demonstrated outside of the Berks County Detention Center, an immigration detention center, in Leesport (Pennsylvania) to call for the release of all women currently detained in the center instead of their transfer upon the closure of the center in January 2023. Members of CASA, Shut Down Berks Coalition, Aldea - the People's Justice Center, and Make the Road Pennsylvania participated in the demonstration which was organized by the Cabrini University Center on Immigration.

On 6 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside of the Autoneum AG factory in Bloomsburg (Pennsylvania) to call for higher wages and improved health care costs. The picket took place on day 6 of their strike organized by Workers United Local 1700, an affiliate of the SEIU.

On 6 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator. The protest was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey.

On 5 December 2022, about two dozen people rallied outside of the Old Main building on the Pennsylvania State University campus in State College (Pennsylvania) to call for the University to drop their disciplinary proceedings against a student protester who was arrested at an October 2022 protest against an event featuring Gavin McInnes at the University. The protest was organized by the Student Committee for Defense and Solidarity.

On 5 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside of the Autoneum AG factory in Bloomsburg (Pennsylvania) to call for higher wages and improved health care costs. The picket took place on day 5 of their strike organized by Workers United Local 1700, an affiliate of the SEIU.

On 4 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside of the Autoneum AG factory in Bloomsburg (Pennsylvania) to call for higher wages and improved health care costs. The picket took place on day 4 of their strike organized by Workers United Local 1700, an affiliate of the SEIU.

On 3 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside of the Autoneum AG factory in Bloomsburg (Pennsylvania) to call for higher wages and improved health care costs. The picket took place on day 3 of their strike organized by Workers United Local 1700, an affiliate of the SEIU.

On 2 December 2022, an unreported number of people picketed outside of the Autoneum AG factory in Bloomsburg (Pennsylvania) to call for higher wages and improved health care costs. The picket took place on day 2 of their strike organized by Workers United Local 1700, an affiliate of the SEIU.

On 2 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. Members of the AFL-CIO and Pennsylvania State Education Association (an affiliate of the NEA) visited the picket which took place as part of day 46 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 2 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated on the Pennsylvania State University campus in State College (Pennsylvania) in support of the anti-lockdown demonstrations in China and to call for the Chinese Communist Party to relinquish power. Chinese students and members of the Chinese community participated in the demonstration which was organized by Penn State Students for Hong Kong.

On 1 December 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. A representative of Communications Workers of America Local 14827 visited the picket which took place as part of day 45 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 30 November 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated in Pittsburgh (Pennsylvania) to call for the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette to return to the negotiating table to give workers a better contract. Workers represented by Communications Workers of America Locals 14842 and 14827, Teamsters Local 205/211, and Pressmen's Union Local 24M/9N (which is a part of the Teamsters) who make up the Post-Gazette's distribution, advertising, and production divisions joined the picket which took place as part of day 44 of their strike which was organized by the Pittsburgh News Guild, a member of the CWA.

On 30 November 2022, more than 400 people gathered on the Pennsylvania State University campus in State College (Pennsylvania) to demonstrate in opposition to the death of Mahsa Amini in Iran as well as in remembrance of all those who died during the protests in Iran. Members of the Penn State Iranian Student Association participated in the demonstration which took place as part of a worldwide series of demonstrations organized by the Iranian Scholars for Liberty.

On 30 November 2022, an unreported number of people gathered on the Pennsylvania State University campus in State College (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the University's use of Nike to make their college apparel in response to the discovery of labor rights violations in Thailand. The protest was organized by the Penn State Chapter of United Students Against Sweatshops.

On 29 November 2022, an unreported number of people demonstrated outside of Sen. Pat Toomey's office in Philadelphia (Pennsylvania) in opposition to the Senator. The protest was organized by Tuesdays with Toomey.

On 29 November 2022, more than 200 people gathered along Centre Avenue in Reading (Pennsylvania) to call for action to address a rise in a hatred for marginalized groups and restrict access to high-powered weapons as well as to honor those who died in the 19 November Club Q, an LGBT+ club, shooting in Colorado Springs, Colorado, especially one of the victims who was from the area. A Protestant Christian pastor, State Senator Judy Schwank (D), Reading Mayor Eddie Moran (D), members of the man's family, and members of the LGBT Center of Greater Reading participated in the vigil.
